title: Navigating Challenges and Technical Debt in LLMs Deployment: Ahmed Menshawy
talk_summary: A Mastercard AI leader argues that the ML/LLM code is under 5-10% of an end-to-end GenAI pipeline, with the surrounding data, access-control, retrieval, and infrastructure work dominating effort and technical debt. He frames RAG as the fix for hallucination, staleness, attribution, and revision, but stresses that production RAG requires jointly optimizing retriever and generator and preserving enterprise access controls.

takeaways.technique: Treat retrieval and generation as one coupled system, not two blind brains
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of bolting a vector store onto a frozen model, they note the original RAG paper trains retriever and generator in parallel so the generator learns to use retrieved evidence; they say this needs open model weights.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the actual rag paper ... is actually about training these two in in parallel

takeaways.technique: Per-task scoped access instead of one global all-data agent
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist enterprise access controls be preserved inside the LLM ecosystem, using specialized models per task rather than a single global system with access to everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to maintain the same access controls and and have certain specialized models that can work for certain tasks

takeaways.technique: Budget for the 90% around the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite the NIPS pipeline chart showing ML code is <5% of an end-to-end system and their own paper showing >90% of LLM-app work is outside the model call: data collection, access control, safeguards, infra.
takeaways.numbers: ML code <5% of end-to-end pipeline; surrounding work >90%

takeaways.what_they_do: They enumerate concrete LLM failure modes enterprises hit in production: hallucination, attribution, staleness, revision/opt-out, customization, and inference-vs-training compute growth.
